RagShortTexts: Counterweight trebuchets revolutionized sieges, launching massive boulders using box ballast.

Variants.Content: By the mid-13th century, the counterweight trebuchet eclipsed human-powered traction engines. Using a pivoted beam loaded with tons of earth and scrap metal inside a swinging counterpoise, it hurls 300-pound dressed masonry balls on flat trajectories to shatter thick curtain walls.

Castles now require massive sloping taluses at their base to deflect plunging boulders. A master siege engineer and his crew of timber-wrights are worth more during an investment than fifty heavy cavalry.

Nothing chills the blood like the groaning ratchet of a siege engine's windlass. When a three-hundred-pound rock strikes the parapet, flying stone splinters will butcher men faster than a volley of arrows.
